messages:
anna: quick q — how do we want to handle required indicators on the dense Create Endpoint form? asterisks feel terse. mike: i'd vote for readable "Required" text on labels in dense views. Asterisk only is too easy to miss and isn't great for a11y. jamal: +1. Also if we must keep a visual asterisk, ensure the accessible name includes the word 'required' so screen readers don't rely on visual cues. lexi: technical note: for screen readers include either visible text 'Required' in the label or add an aria-label like `label + ' (required)'`. Avoid purely decorative asterisks. sam: i18n reminder: the word 'Required' must be a token so translators can change order/punctuation. don't hardcode English in the DOM. anna: good call. Now about error surface: inline field errors vs a top-of-step summary for cross-field issues? mike: inline for single-field (invalid email, too short). top summary when validation involves multiple fields or sequencing conflicts (e.g., retention < min retention elsewhere). Keeps inline focused. jamal: implement both but ensure the summary is keyboard-focusable and includes links that move focus to the specific input. pattern: summary > link to input id. lexi: also avoid layout shift — reserve the helper/error line under inputs so toggling an error doesn't push content. CSS: `.helper { min-height: 1.25rem; }`. mike: and `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby` linking to the error element. Example: `input aria-describedby="endpoint-url-error" aria-invalid="true"`. anna: destructive confirmation patterns? typed confirm for every delete is painful on phones. Thoughts on scope-based rules? jamal: scope-based makes sense: typed confirm only for org-level destructive actions (delete org model, purge customer data). For per-user/resource deletes, use modal with clear heading, summary copy, and a secondary checkbox like `I understand this cannot be undone`. sam: mobile UX: checkbox + CTA is much faster. typed confirm requires keyboard entry which is slow on phones. so reserve typed confirm for a small subset. lexi: accessibility: if we use typed confirm, don't rely on placeholder text; provide a visible label and ensure mismatches are announced with `role="alert"`. sample snippet: ```html
Text does not match
``` mike: another nit: if we show 'Required' text on labels, we should use a lower-contrast token to prevent visual noise on long forms. maybe `color: token.text.subtle` vs bold red. anna: decision proposal to ship in the next component patch: 1) show explicit 'Required' word on labels (tokenized for i18n), 2) inline errors for single-field validations with reserved helper space, 3) top-of-step summary for cross-field errors with focusable links, 4) typed-confirm only for org-scoped destructive actions; checkbox-confirm for user-scoped, 5) add `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` and `role=alert` patterns in the docs. jamal: small implementation ask: can frontend add a tiny test harness showing dense vs expanded label behavior? helps PMs and translators preview. mike: i'll open a PR with examples and the CSS helper reserve. will include code for the summary-to-field focus links. design-bot: created issue https://redwood.internals/issue/4278 — "forms: required marker + inline+summary + scoped typed-confirm" :white_check_mark: anna: perfect, i'll update the figma tokens and modal variants after the PR lands. thanks all :thumbsup:
